notes.claim: Phasors are good for summing sinusoids of the same frequency.
The sum of the y projections of the component phasors is the y projection of the sum of the component phasors, which is why phasor addition gives the sum wave.
Sinusoids of different frequencies cannot be shown on the same phasor diagram, because the vectors turn at different speeds.
The MCA Marine Electro-technology syllabus covers explaining phasors and solving graphical problems adding and subtracting ac voltages and currents by the phasor method.
Three-phase systems consist of three voltages equal in magnitude and 120 degrees out of phase with each other.
The square root of three in three-phase systems is a magnitude multiplier that comes from adding or subtracting two equal vectors 120 degrees apart.
At 230 V phase voltage, the three-phase line voltage is described as 400 V, not twice 230 V.
Whether a phasor's length is the peak or the rms value depends on the convention used.
notes.contested: Electronics Tutorials says a vector's magnitude is the peak value while a phasor's is the rms value; UNSW Physclips says rms phasor diagrams have the same shape as amplitude ones, scaled by 0.71.
